We cannot integrate the given integral because we cannot find a simple antiderivative of the integrand. So, we change the order of integration.

We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{1}\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,y\le z\le 1}
$$

The region $R$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/b486ea542dc330a483fa76f333ab80c9fcd07434db5dc0c5a0a62a335294f127.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/b626c20c336bc81df9194f161998f7c6aea524a11495fede615cdf76f5d93f59.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

- The right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=y\,⟹\,y=z.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7386453aebec047469c829e2c2c5d6c4ab915ac965bbcd39838dc7be50941d54.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane with the bottom curve given by $z=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/4b2bb3583b5c0807c653f503cdf9ed954f38db8a30eef548738e96cedb889288.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{1}\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}\,dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{z}\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}[y]_{0}^{z}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}z\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}z\sqrt{1-{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{1}{3}{(1-{z}^{2})}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[x]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
